Native North Carolinian here, currently living in Raleigh. I would definitely recommend it. While yes, it does get hot in the summer here, it's not hot like Texas (100's are pretty rare here). We do get snow occasionally, but definitely not every year (average snowfall for Raleigh is ~7 inches per year but we usually get a good snow every 3-5 years). Relatively mild climate and we actually do have all 4 seasons (usually).

The triangle area, including Raleigh, Durham, and Chapel Hill, is one of the most progressive areas in the state and likely in the South as well. Several world class schools here including NC State, UNC-Chapel Hill (aka UNC) and Duke. RTP offers lots of good jobs especially in the tech sector. Plenty of outdoor activities can be pursued nearly year-round due to the mild climate. Raleigh has lots of parks and a good greenway walking trail system. Also several good entertainment venues for live shows as well as museums and other more 'cultured' attractions. Plus, Raleigh is about 0.99 CLI (close to average cost of living, comparatively)

Access is great too. 2.5 hours and you're on the beach, 3.5 and on top of a (small-ish) mountain. Accessible to I-40 as a major east-west thoroughfare and I-95 for north-south. Generally good roads but poor public transportation options, even in the city.

Keep in mind, though, Raleigh is a population of just over 300k so not a big city like DC, Honolulu or Houston. But a great place to live and work, in my opinion (but I'm totally biased).

I'm a DC area resident, and a lot of my family is from the El Paso TX area. DC weather is moderate and varies throughout the year (though fairly moist, but not Seattle moist). El Paso has a very hot and dry climate with a lot of Mexican culture. I can't really speak for any of those other places though, but for the most part it would depend on what you do for a living, what you are looking for, etc.
